chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saif, from his brother Ali ibn Saif, from his father Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Muhammad ibn Marid, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan, who said: I said to Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, people narrate a hadith that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Narrate from the Children of Israel and there is no blame."

He said: Yes. I said: So shall we narrate from the Children of Israel with what we have heard, and there is no blame upon us? He said: Have you not heard what he said: "It is sufficient for a man to be a liar that he narrates everything he hears." I said: So how is that? He said: Whatever is in the Book (Quran) that something was among the Children of Israel, then you narrate that it is present in this nation, and there is no blame.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct understanding of narrating from the Children of Israel in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this dialogue to resolve the apparent contradiction between the general permission to narrate Isra'iliyyat and the caution against uncritical transmission. Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the 'no blame' ruling applies specifically when attributing historical events or traits of the Children of Israel to the current Ummah is supported by explicit Quranic evidence, thereby establishing a rigorous standard for theological application rather than mere storytelling.
